newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss cabinet approves investment plan, tax reform.
newsitem.headline: Swiss cabinet approves investment plan, tax reform.

text.p: The Swiss cabinet approved plans aimed at enlivening the moribund domestic economy through direct investments and tax reforms, the government economic and finance ministries said in a statement.

The plans call for the federal government to put up 561 million Swiss francs, which will form the nucleus of a 2.4 billion franc total investment package. The plan also encompasses spending from Swiss regional governments.
The measures still require approval of the federal parliament, which is set to discuss them at the end of April.
"By giving a temporary stimulus to demand, the investment programme will accelerate a recovery from economic stagnation which has lasted for six years," the ministries said.
"The federal government's additional spending of 561 million francs should stimulate an investment volume of around 2.4 billion francs," the ministries said.
The resulting spending should result in employment of 24,000 people, they added.
The spending will be largely aimed at public works.
The additional investments, according to the ministries, should boost the Swiss gross domestic product (GDP) in 1998 and 1999 by around one-third.
The Swiss GDP was flat in the fourth quarter of 1996, following seven quarters of continued declines. It is expected to grow in 1997 but at a rate below one percent.

In addition, the cabinet approved corporate tax reform which would benefit holding companies as well as smaller and medium-sized companies. It also calls for introducing a flat tax rate of 8.5 percent on corporate earnings, while the so-called "capital tax," the tax imposed on the capital held by a company, would be abolished.
It also calls for lowering the "issue tax," a one-time tax levied on the share capital of new companies issuing shares, to one percent from two percent.
The reforms will lead to an annual revenue loss of 170 million francs. But the government expected positive impulses for Swiss business and higher tax returns as a result.
